tiers: --tier with no tier the runner knows prints the usage, exit 2, runs nothing
tiers: a check file without a tier header on line 2 is refused: no tier header: <path> per file in name order, exit 2, nothing run or written
tiers: each file's timing line ends with its tier: , tier fast or , tier slow
tiers: line 2 is read exactly (a trailing blank refuses it) and a directory named *.sh is refused without a read error
tiers: the slowest: line ends , tier fast, , tier slow, or , tier all for a run without --tier
tmux: TMUX_KEEP_HOURS=0: the driver window saves its scrollback and kills h-<run> when the driver exits
tmux: a keep window keeps h-<run>, its supervisor window gone, the scrollback saved; a Ctrl-C there still closes it
tmux: run id dot.run gets session h-dot-run, gone at keep 0
treekey --names: the entries' names in map order (a duplicate path merged into the first), exit 1 and no line for a path no entry has
treekey --partial --names: --partial's lines, then one ': <path> <names…>' line per entry (a duplicate path merged), map order
treekey --partial: a CLAUDE.md-only change moves the full key (16 hex), keeps the reduced key, and differs in CLAUDE.md's blob line only
treekey --partial: a dropped entry (directory, no name, outside the tree, under an ignored prefix) is one stderr line each; the output is the map's without it
treekey --partial: a mapped path absent from the tree is a `- <path>` line, in map order
treekey.mjs exports ignoreList, parseMap, treeKey, partialKeys and mapNames, pure on a fixed file list and blobs
treekey.mjs parseListing: a clean regular file keeps its index blob; a stale, unmerged, symlink, gitlink, assume-unchanged, skip-worktree or untracked row has none; one row per index entry
treekey.mjs: --partial's full key, reduced key and blob lines equal the definition's, a mapped file clean, edited, absent and deleted
treekey.mjs: a clean tree starts one git and no hash-object; a dirty one a second, once, for whatever number of files
treekey.mjs: a name with a quote or a newline: the definition's key from the index, and edited never a stale key: its own, or the throw check.sh reads as a full run
treekey.mjs: an unmerged path keeps its one row per stage and the worktree's blob, a gitlink is no file, as the definition has them
treekey.mjs: below the repo's top a clean tree still has no key (the throw check.sh reads as a full run, no marker), as a dirty one
treekey.mjs: main reads the environment from io.env at call time: two --pathspec answers in one process
treekey.mjs: main runs git in io.cwd: the key, --partial --names and --pathspec are the bytes the CLI prints inside that repo, from another cwd
treekey.mjs: main's git gets io.env (git config set on the call moves what ls-files leaves out)
treekey.mjs: the key equals its definition after each change to a tree: edits staged and not, deletions, untracked and ignored files, symlinks, a mode, a touch, the run record
treekey: a map whose every entry is dropped is as no map (two lines); the bare call never parses the map (no stderr)
treekey: an absolute or .. entry is dropped, not an error (the key is docs/plans' alone)
treekey: entries are literal path prefixes (. and globs leave nothing out; ./docs/plans/ is docs/plans)
treekey: two trees that differ only under an ignored prefix have the same 16-hex key; a change under lib/ changes it
treekey: without a map --partial prints two equal keys and no blob line; the bare call is one line, --partial's line 1, map or not

xtrace: HARNESS_XTRACE=<dir> traces the CLI, the driver, a lane and the check runner, lines led by +<file>:<line>:
xtrace: a directory that can't be made, or can't be written, costs the trace, never the command
xtrace: a run started in tmux traces its driver too: the CLI passes the variable to the tmux command
xtrace: a run without HARNESS_XTRACE leaves no trace file, and no trace line in its output
xtrace: a sourced file's lines are traced under its own name, by the process that sourced it (lib/record.sh)
xtrace: a trace file is its owner's to read and nobody else's (it holds what the commands held, a token among it)
xtrace: a traced segment's first note says where the trace goes; a plain run has no such note
xtrace: every executable script of lib/ and bin/harness sources lib/xtrace.sh under the guard, once
xtrace: the trace goes to its own descriptor: the traced run's output holds no trace line
xtrace: the traced run's harness-log.md is the plain run's plus that note, the run id, times, hashes and lengths aside
